sections.overview: Taenaris urania is a nymphalid butterfly recorded from the Moluccan Islands of Indonesia.
sections.identification: Like other Taenaris, it belongs to a group of large butterflies with conspicuous eyespots on the hindwings.
sections.habitat: Museum specimens document it on several Moluccan islands, but the sources consulted do not define its habitat in detail.
sections.diet: A review reports that adult Taenaris butterflies feed on fermenting fruit and sap; species-specific diet data remain limited.
sections.behavior: Species-specific behavior is sparsely documented in the sources consulted.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide a verified account of this species’ breeding cycle.
sections.ecology: Taenaris urania is the type species of its genus, which is placed among the brush-footed butterflies (Nymphalidae).
sections.conservation: The sources consulted do not report a global conservation assessment for Taenaris urania.
